stem: What was one effect of this new style of "musical Western" on the United States in the 1930s?

options.label: F
options.text: Country music became more popular than rock and roll music.

options.label: G
options.text: Country music prompted people to move to farms on the Great Plains.

options.label: H
options.text: Country music transitioned from a regional genre to a national sensation.

options.label: J
options.text: Country music encouraged Exodusters to migrate from southern states.

visual_elements: [Gene Autry] got a bit part in [In Old Santa Fe], a Western in 1934, and unbelievably the ideas that came from this Western . . . pretty much started the template of the musical Western. Audiences just loved them—they had the music, they had the comedy and, of course, the action and those great fancy cowboy outfits, too. —"Gene Autry, America’s 'Public Cowboy No. 1'," National Public Radio, www.npr.org (accessed November 20, 2018)
